approved: Introduced debate on the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill, explaining it repeals unused pay slip superannuation reporting provisions from the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Act 1993, and removes the requirement for associates of a person seeking more than a 15 per cent stake in a financial sector company to separately seek Treasurer approval.

Supported the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill on behalf of Labor, noting superannuation savings held by Australians saved the budget about $6 billion last financial year alone, and said Australia's national savings pool now stands at more than $1.85 trillion, giving it around the fifth largest pool of funds under management in the world.

Supported the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill, recalling the Prime Minister's election-night declaration that Australia is under new management and open for business, and noted 70 per cent of employees who do not receive their superannuation entitlement do not complain to the Australian Taxation Office until after leaving that employer.

Criticised the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill as part of the government's repeal day stunt, disputing its claim of achieving up to $1 billion in compliance cost savings through what he called repeal day theatrics.

Supported the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill, noting three separate acts currently require employers to report superannuation entitlements on pay slips, and explained the bill's new definition of Australia for tax purposes covers seabeds and resources such as oil and gas beneath the Joint Petroleum Development Area in the Timor Sea.

Criticised the government's repeal day rhetoric during debate on the Treasury Legislation Amendment Bill, contrasting it with recent valedictory tributes to Gough Whitlam and former Queensland Treasurer Wayne Goss, and dubbed the legislation the Turning Up For Work Day Bill.
Opened his remarks on the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill by noting the member for Moreton had just delivered a lengthy critical speech despite ultimately supporting the legislation.

Argued that the bill's measures were useful but ordinary parliamentary work rather than a major deregulation achievement. Supported simplifying tax laws and criticised the proposed repeal of pay-slip superannuation reporting, warning that unpaid contributions could leave workers without expected retirement or insurance protections.

Argued that the bill delivered practical results by removing 10,000 regulations on the first repeal day and another thousand subsequently, amounting to around $2 billion in regulatory reductions. Supported provisions concerning superannuation, tax administration and the definition of Australia, and urged South Australia to pursue similar deregulation measures.

Paid tribute to Phillip Hughes, then supported the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill 2014, saying the government has cut $2.1 billion in red tape this year including scrapping nearly 1,000 pieces of legislation totalling 7,200 pages, and quoted Penrith small business owner John Capes describing spending more than 10 hours a week on compliance paperwork.

Supported the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill 2014, arguing that red tape and over-regulation stifle small business and productivity, and cited Australia's ranking of 124th out of 148 countries on the World Economic Forum's burden of government regulation index.

Supported the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill 2014, describing government efforts to cut red tape for small business including simplified APRA compliance measures projected to save $13.4 million, and welcomed changes to government procurement and the Franchising Code of Conduct meant to help small and medium enterprises.

Supported the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill 2014, saying the government has now cut $2 billion in red tape, and detailed the bill's four schedules covering superannuation payslip reporting, consolidated tax provisions, and a single definition of Australia for tax purposes.

Supported the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill 2014, citing an Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry survey in which 79.7 per cent of businesses raised major or moderate concerns about company tax, and proposed reviving an income-tax-sharing arrangement between the Commonwealth and the states.

Supported the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill 2014, said the government's two repeal days have together reduced compliance costs by more than $2.1 billion, and detailed the bill's repeal of superannuation payslip reporting requirements that would have imposed extra costs on employers.

Supported the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill 2014, and described how a Longman leather manufacturer had been forced to pay up to $20,000 to get an imported tanning chemical approved despite it meeting international standards, before regulators agreed to accept such international risk assessments.

Supported the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill 2014, framed it within the government's deregulation agenda that has cut more than $2.1 billion in compliance costs, and listed local benefits for pharmacies and training providers in the Forde electorate.

Supported the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill 2014, praised the member for Braddon and fellow Tasmanian MPs, and referenced Liberal Party founder Robert Menzies' 1946 slogan about wanting fewer forms and more reforms.

Spoke in support of the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill 2014, listed several coalition members who had spoken on it, and noted that no opposition members appeared on the speaking list, suggesting Labor was not interested in debating the bill.

Supported the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill 2014, arguing that repealing red tape would improve productivity and address budget pressures. Reported around $13.5 billion in annual interest, over $1 billion a month in interest and 21,000 new or additional regulations, and said small businesses were overburdened by compliance.

Supported the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill 2014, saying the government has exceeded its election promise to cut $1 billion in red and green tape annually, now delivering over $2 billion, with nearly 1,000 pieces of regulation and 7,200 pages removed in this round alone, building on the first repeal day's removal of over 10,000 pieces and 50,000 pages worth $700 million in compliance costs.

Criticised government members for treating all regulation as inherently bad during debate on the repeal day bill, arguing that countries like Gabon and the Dominican Republic, which lack sophisticated legal and administrative structures, are not economic success stories, and said a proper legal framework is essential for business to thrive.

Supported the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill as part of the government's broader deregulation agenda, said the government had more than doubled its target with a net reduction of over $2.1 billion in compliance costs, and noted Australia ranked 124th out of 148 countries in the World Economic Forum's regulatory burden index.

Summed up debate on the Treasury Legislation Amendment (Repeal Day) Bill, which repeals payslip superannuation reporting requirements, consolidates duplicated tax administration provisions into the Taxation Administration Act 1953, and removes the requirement for associates without a direct shareholding above 15 per cent in a financial sector company to separately seek approval.
